newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans mostly down on good weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans mostly down on good weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were mostly lower early Friday, under pressure from prospects for good growing weather this weekend, traders said.
"It's going to be a greenhouse this weekend," said one trader.
Forecasters were calling for the hottest temperatures of the year on Friday, with highs in the 90s (degrees Fahrenheit) from Nebraska to Illinois and upper 80s in Ohio and Indiana.
Widespread rains were also expected this weekend.
Traders also were awaiting July options expiration at 1201 CDT. Trade in July could be volatile up to that point.
The market shrugged off reports that China purchased up to 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for November shipment overnight.
In early trade, Refco sold 500,000 bushels July, ADM was a seller in November, and Term Commodities and Smith Barney each bought 500,000 bushels July, pit sources said.
At 0957 CDT, July soybeans were down 1/2 cent per bushel at $8.37, and other months were 6-1/2 cents lower to 1/4 higher.
